nodes.statement: Given quantum states rho,sigma on a Hilbert space CMcalH with dimension N, such that supp(rho) subset supp(sigma). Alice is given the eigen-decomposition of rho and Bob is given the eigen-decomposition of sigma. Let relentrhosigma and varepsilon >0 be known to Alice and Bob. There exists an entanglement assisted quantum one-way communication protocol, with Alice sending CMcalO(relentrhosigma+1)/varepsilon^4) bits of communication to Bob, such that the state tilderho that Bob outputs at the end of the protocol satisfies F(rho,tilderho)geq 1-5varepsilon .

\end{enumerate}
\end{mdframed}

\[\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}+2\delta}{f}\leq \CMcal{O}((c+1)/\delta^9),\]

\[\dqcc{, \mu^k}{{\varepsilon}}{f^k}\geq\Omega \br{k \br{\delta^9\cdot\dqcc{, \mu}{{\varepsilon}+\delta}{f}-1}}.\]

Let M be performed by Alice on the joint system A_1A_2 with outcome I in [w] and by Bob on the joint system B_1B_2 with outcome J in [w]. Then Pr[I = J] geq left(1-sqrtonenormrho-sigma - frac14onenormrho-sigma^2right)^3.

We assume that a_1, ldots, a_N, b_1, ldots b_N are rational numbers and let K be the least common multiple of their denominators. The error due to this assumption goes to 0 as K rightarrow infty. Introduce registers A_1,B_1 associated to CMcalH and registers A_2,B_2 associated to some Hilbert space CMcalH' with an orthonormal basis setket1,ket2ldots ketK. Consider the following state shared in A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2. ketS_A_1B_1A_2B_2 ensuremath stackreldef= frac1sqrtKNsum_i=1^N keti,i_A_1B_1 otimes left(sum_m=1^Kketm, m_A_2B_2 right) For brevity, define the registers Aensuremath stackreldef= A_1A_2 and B ensuremath stackreldef= B_1B_2. The protocol is described below. Input: Alice is given rho=sum_i=1^Na_iketbraa_i. Bob is given sigma=sum_i=1^Nb_iketbrab_i. Shared resources: Alice and Bob hold infinitely many registers A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i (i>0), such that A_1^iequiv A_1, A^i_2equiv A_2, B_1^iequiv B_1,B_2^iequiv B_2. The shared state in register A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i is ketS_A_1^iA_2^iB_1^iB_2^i. Let A equiv A_1A_2 and Bequiv B_1B_2 be used as output registers. Let i refer to the `index' of corresponding registers. item For each i>0, Alice performs the measurement setP_A,I- P_A on the registers A^i_1A^i_2, where P_Aensuremath stackreldef= sum_iketa_i_A_1braa_i_A_1otimes left(sum_m=1^Ka_iketm_A_2bram_A_2right) She declares success if she obtains outcome corresponding to P_A. She stops once she succeeds in some register A^j, and swaps A^j with A. item For each i>0, Bob performs the measurement setP_B,I- P_B on the registers B^i_1B^i_2, where P_Bensuremath stackreldef= sum_iketb_i_B_1brab_i_B_1otimes left(sum_m=1^Kb_iketm_B_2bram_B_2right) He declares success if he obtains outcome corresponding to P_B. He stops once he succeeds in some register B^j, and swaps B^j with B. At the end of above protocol, let the joint state in the register AB be tau. The following claim shows the first part of the theorem. ensuremath Tr _A_2B_1B_2(tau)=rho and ensuremath Tr _A_1A_2B_2(tau)=sigma. It is easily seen that the marginal of the state (P_A otimes I_B) ketS in register A is rho. Similarly the marginal of the state (I_A otimes P_B) ketS in register B in is sigma. Following series of claims establish second part of the theorem. tau geq frac(P_Aotimes P_B)ketSbraS(P_Aotimes P_B) 1 - braS (I_A-P_A)otimes(I_B-P_B)ketS enspace . Consider the event that Alice and Bob succeed at the same index. The resulting state in AA_1BB_1 is frac(P_Aotimes P_B ) ketSbraS (P_Aotimes P_B)braS(P_A otimes P_B)ketS, and this event occurs with probability sum_i=0^inftybraS(I_A-P_A)otimes(I_B-P_B)ketS^i cdot braS(P_A otimes P_B)ketS= fracbraS(P_A otimes P_B)ketS1 - braS(I_A-P_A)otimes(I_B-P_B)ketS. Since the cases of Bob succeeding before Alice and Alice succeeding before Bob add positive operators to tau, we get the desired. Let kettheta ensuremath stackreldef= frac(P_Aotimes P_A)ketSnorm(P_Aotimes P_A)ketS. Then brathetataukettheta geq fracleft(1-sqrtonenormrho-sigma - frac14onenormrho-sigma^2right)^21 + sqrtonenormrho-sigma - frac14onenormrho-sigma^2 geq left(1-sqrtonenormrho-sigma - frac14onenormrho-sigma^2right)^3 . Consider, brathetataukettheta &geq frac absbrathetaP_Aotimes P_BketS^21 - braS (I_A-P_A)otimes(I_B-P_B)ketS & mbox(Claim~)\\ & = frac absbrathetaP_Aotimes P_BketS^22/N-braSP_Aotimes P_BketS & mbox(using braSP_Aotimes I_BketS=braSI_Aotimes P_BketS=1/N). Define R_ijensuremath stackreldef= a_i absbraketa_ib_j^2 and R'_ijensuremath stackreldef= b_i absbraketa_ib_j^2. Note that both \R_ij\ and \R'_ij\ form probability distributions over [N^2]. Also note that F(R,R') = ensuremath Tr (sqrtrhosqrtsigma). Consider (using relation between fidelity and ell_1 distance, Facts~ and~), sum_i,jmin(R_ij,R'_i,j) & = 1 - frac12onenormR-R' geq 1 - sqrt1-F(R,R')^2 nonumber \\ &= 1 - sqrt1-(ensuremath Tr sqrtrhosqrtsigma)^2 geq 1-sqrtonenormrho-sigma - frac14onenormrho-sigma^2 . Combining Equations~ and~ we get the desired. Let M=\M_1,M_2ldots M_w\ be a projective measurement in the support of A_1A_2. Let E=sum_i=1^w M_iotimes M_i. Then ensuremath Tr (E ketbratheta) = 1. Since M_i is a projector in the support of A_1A_2, we have (M_iotimes M_i)kettheta = (M_iotimes I)kettheta. Hence, \[brathetaEkettheta=sum_ibrathetaM_iotimes M_ikettheta = sum_ibrathetaM_iotimes Ikettheta = 1 . tag*qedhere \] Finally using monotonicity of fidelity under quantum operation (Fact~) and Claim~ we get the second part of the theorem as follows. \[sqrtensuremath Tr (Etau) geq F(tau , ketbratheta) = sqrtbrathetataukettheta geq left(1-sqrtonenormrho-sigma - frac14onenormrho-sigma^2right)^3/2 . tag*qedhere \]

\begin{align*}
\bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} &\geq   \frac{ \abs{\bra{\theta}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}}^2}{1 - \bra{S} (I_A-P_A)\otimes(I_B-P_B)\ket{S}} &  \mbox{(Claim~\ref{claim:tau})}\\ 
& = \frac{ \abs{\bra{\theta}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}}^2}{2/N-\bra{S}P_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}} & \mbox{(using $\bra{S}P_A\otimes I_B\ket{S}=\bra{S}I_A\otimes P_B\ket{S}=1/N$)}.
\end{align*}

By direct calculation, we get 
$$(P_A\otimes P_B)\ket{S}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{KN}}\sum_{i,j}\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\braket{b_j}{a_i}\ket{b_j}\sum_{m=1}^{K\min(a_i,b_j)}\ket{m,m} ;$$ 
$$\ket{\theta}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{K}}\sum_i\ket{\conjugate{a_i}}\ket{a_i}\sum_{m=1}^{Ka_i}\ket{m,m} .$$ 
Hence,
\begin{equation} \label{eq:thetatau}\bra{\theta}\tau\ket{\theta} \geq \frac{\left(\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2\right)^2}{2-\sum_{i,j}\min(a_i,b_j) \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2} .
\end{equation}

Define $R_{ij}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } a_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2$ and $R'_{ij}\ensuremath{ \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} } b_i \abs{\braket{a_i}{b_j}}^2$. Note that both $\{R_{ij}\}$ and $\{R'_{ij}\}$ form probability distributions over $[N^2]$. Also note that $\mathrm{F}(R,R') = \ensuremath{ \mathrm{Tr} }(\sqrt{\rho}\sqrt{\sigma})$. Consider (using relation between fidelity and $\ell_1$ distance, Facts~\ref{fact:fidelityvstrace} and~\ref{fact:tracefidelityequi}),
\begin{align}
 \sum_{i,j}\min(R_{ij},R'_{i,j}) & = 1 - \frac{1}{2}\onenorm{R-R'}  \geq 1 - \sqrt{1-\mathrm{F}(R,R')^2} \nonumber \\
